title: 1.1: Reports that libharfbuzz is loaded into the main Kitty process for text shaping (e.g., via ldd output showing libharfbuzz.so)
1.2: Reports that libfreetype is loaded into the main Kitty process for glyph rendering (e.g., via ldd output showing libfreetype.so)

1.3: Reports that fast_data_types.so is loaded into the main Kitty process as its core C extension module (e.g., listed in /proc/<pid>/maps, or stack frames such as io_loop or talk_loop resolving to fast_data_types.so)

1.4: Reports measured per-thread activity at idle and under stress, showing which threads become busy (e.g., KittyChildMon and the main kitty thread near zero at idle and consuming large CPU shares under stress, from /proc/<pid>/task/*/stat ticks or top -H)

1.5: Describes a portability-versus-performance tradeoff tied to an observed runtime artifact (e.g., only glfw-x11.so loaded out of the per-platform GLFW backends, or Mesa's llvmpipe software rasterizer threads consuming CPU because no GPU is available)
1.6: Reports that Kitty's control interface remains accessible during rendering pressure (e.g., via kitten @ ls command)
1.7: Reports that kitten runs as a separate process with its own PID, not loaded into the main Kitty process
1.8: Reports that the kitten executable is built with Go (e.g., by showing Go-specific ELF sections like .gosymtab or .gopclntab)
1.9: Reports a stack-level or symbol-level snapshot captured during stress (e.g., via gdb backtrace, nm symbols, or similar inspection)
1.10: Reports that C handles font shaping and rasterization (e.g., via HarfBuzz hb_shape or FreeType FT_* calls)

1.11: Reports that Python handles configuration, orchestration, or remote control in Kitty (e.g., kitty/main.py starting the app before calling into the C main loop, or kitty/rc/*.py modules serving remote-control commands)
1.12: Reports that Go is used for kitten utilities that run as separate processes
2.1: Claims that Python directly calls OpenGL rendering functions
2.2: Presents conclusions about the Python, C and Go split without any supporting output collected from a running Kitty (e.g., relying only on reading source files)
2.3: Claims that kitten communicates with Kitty through shared memory other than graphics-protocol image transfers or probes
